sections.heading: 🔍 What is Electrical Surgical Unit Testing?
paragraphs: An Electrosurgical Unit (ESU) is a critical device used in modern surgeries to cut tissue or coagulate bleeding using high-frequency electric currents. Proper testing of these units is vital for clinical safety, regulatory compliance, and device performance.

At ITC India, we offer comprehensive ESU in accordance with IEC 60601-2-2, ensuring that each device meets international safety and performance standards. Electrical Surgical Unit (ESU) Testing Services

sections.heading: 🔬 Key Tests Conducted on Electrosurgical Units
paragraphs: We follow IEC 60601-2-2 and IEC 60601-1 for device-specific and general safety testing.

rows: Ensures patient safety from unintended current
Confirms power output within acceptable tolerance
Evaluates the shape and peak of the output wave
Verifies mode functions for precision surgery
Tests contact quality monitoring for burns risk
Ensures electromagnetic compatibility with other equipment

sections.heading: 🛠️ How It Works- Electrical Surgical Unit (ESU) Testing Services
bullets: Connection Setup: The active output from the ESU is connected to a dummy load, simulating tissue resistance.
Monitoring Neutral Electrode: The return (neutral) electrode is connected to monitor unintended leakage.
Analyzer Testing: Fluke QA-ES III Analyzer, to measure leakage current from the active and neutral lines.
Compliance Validation: We validate that measured leakage is within IEC 60601-2-2 standards:Max active HF leakage: < 150 mA
Max return electrode HF leakage: < 10 mA

sections.heading: ✅ Why This Test is Critical Electrical Surgical Unit (ESU) Testing Services
bullets: Ensures patient safety by verifying no excessive RF currents pass through unintended paths.
Verifies compliance with IEC 60601‑2‑2 standards, essential for CE, FDA, and CDSCO certifications.
Highlights potential degradation in insulation or neutral electrode detection systems over time.
